newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Agie shareholders okay merge with GF unit.
newsitem.headline: Agie shareholders okay merge with GF unit.

text.p: Shareholders in electro-erosion machinery maker Agie Holding AG approved its merger with the Charmilles unit of Swiss engineering group Georg Fischer AG, which has a majority stake in Agie.
An Agie statement said an extraordinary shareholder meeting -- dominated by Georg Fischer -- approved all proposals by the board of directors.
"This finalises the closing of ranks between Agie and Charmilles to form a global leader in electric discharge machine tools working on the spark erosion principle," Agie said.
Georg Fischer said in July it was acquiring a majority stake in Agie and would merge it with unit Charmilles Technologies.
The new company will be called Agie Charmilles Holding AG and will remain listed on the Swiss stock exchange.

"Accumulated sales of the new Agie Charmilles Group for 1996 will approach 800 million Swiss francs, with operating income before interest and taxes around 45 million Swiss francs," the statement said.
Georg Fischer now holds about 78 percent of Agie Charmilles share capital, the statement said.
"The proportion of publicly traded shares is to be increased in the mid term," Agie added.
